question: Under the Nebraska Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, what is the maximum security deposit a landlord may collect from a tenant, exclusive of any separate pet deposit?
choice_a: One and one-half month's periodic rent
choice_b: One month's periodic rent
choice_c: Two months' periodic rent
choice_d: There is no statutory cap in Nebraska
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1416(1) provides that a landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit in an amount or value in excess of one month's periodic rent. This is a hard statutory ceiling under Nebraska's version of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA).

question: In addition to the base security deposit cap, what additional pet deposit may a Nebraska landlord require under §76-1416?
choice_a: Up to one-half of one month's rent
choice_b: A flat $200
choice_c: Up to one-fourth of one month's rent
choice_d: Nebraska law prohibits separate pet deposits
explanation: Section 76-1416(1) allows a landlord to charge an additional pet deposit not exceeding one-fourth of one month's periodic rent, on top of the base security deposit cap of one month's rent.

question: After a Nebraska tenancy terminates, within how many days must the landlord return the security deposit balance along with an itemized statement of any deductions?
choice_a: 7 days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: 14 days
explanation: Section 76-1416(2) requires the landlord to return the security deposit, along with an itemized written statement of any amounts withheld, within fourteen days after the termination of the tenancy and delivery of possession.

question: If a returned security deposit balance is undeliverable to the former tenant, what ultimately happens to those funds under §76-1416?
choice_a: If unclaimed for one year, the balance is treated as abandoned property and reported and paid to the State Treasurer under the Uniform Disposition of Unclaimed Property Act
choice_b: The landlord may keep the funds after 90 days
choice_c: The funds must be donated to a local housing charity
choice_d: The funds escheat immediately to the county where the property is located
explanation: Under §76-1416(2), if the mailed refund is returned as undeliverable, or the balance otherwise remains unclaimed for one year, it is treated as abandoned property that must be reported and paid to the State Treasurer's office in accordance with the Uniform Disposition of Unclaimed Property Act. The landlord cannot simply keep it, and there is no automatic county escheat.

question: If a landlord willfully and in bad faith fails to comply with the security deposit return requirements, what liquidated damages, beyond return of the deposit itself, may the tenant recover under §76-1416(3)?
choice_a: Triple the amount of the deposit
choice_b: One month's periodic rent or two times the amount of the security deposit, whichever is less
choice_c: A flat $500 statutory penalty
choice_d: One month's periodic rent or two times the amount of the security deposit, whichever is greater
explanation: Section 76-1416(3) sets the willful, bad-faith liquidated damages remedy at one month's periodic rent or two times the security deposit amount, whichever is LESS — plus recovery of the deposit, court costs, and attorney's fees. The statute caps the penalty rather than maximizing it.

question: A rental property is sold shortly after a tenant vacates, but before the security deposit has been returned. Under §76-1416(5), who is bound by the obligation to return the deposit?
choice_a: Only the original landlord who originally collected the deposit, regardless of the sale
choice_b: The tenant must pursue only the real estate closing agent who handled the sale
choice_c: The holder of the landlord's interest in the premises at the time the tenancy terminated
choice_d: The obligation is automatically extinguished upon transfer of title
explanation: Section 76-1416(5) provides that the holder of the landlord's interest in the premises at the time of termination of the tenancy is bound by the security deposit provisions, ensuring a new owner cannot escape the prior landlord's deposit-return obligation.

question: Under §76-1425, before a Nebraska tenant may terminate a rental agreement for the landlord's material noncompliance, what notice must the tenant give?
choice_a: The tenant may terminate immediately with no notice
choice_b: A 3-day pay-or-quit style notice
choice_c: Verbal notice followed by a 60-day waiting period
choice_d: Written notice specifying the breach, stating the agreement will terminate not less than 30 days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied within 14 days
explanation: Section 76-1425 requires the tenant to give written notice specifying the breach; the landlord then has 14 days to cure it, and if uncured, the rental agreement terminates on a date not less than 30 days after the tenant's notice was received.

question: Under §76-1425, if the same type of breach by the landlord recurs within a certain number of months after an earlier notice and cure, the tenant may terminate on just 14 days' written notice without a further cure period. What is that time window?
choice_a: 6 months
choice_b: 3 months
choice_c: 9 months
choice_d: 12 months
explanation: Section 76-1425 provides that if substantially the same breach recurs within six months, the tenant may terminate the rental agreement on at least 14 days' written notice, without giving the landlord another opportunity to cure.

question: Under §76-1427, if a Nebraska landlord fails to supply heat, running water, hot water, or other essential services, what self-help remedy is a tenant permitted to use?
choice_a: The tenant may withhold the entire rent payment indefinitely
choice_b: The tenant may procure reasonable amounts of the essential service and deduct the actual cost from rent
choice_c: The tenant must first obtain a court order before taking any action
choice_d: The tenant may terminate the lease immediately with no notice to the landlord
explanation: Section 76-1427 lets a tenant, after proper written notice, procure reasonable amounts of hot water, running water, heat, and other essential services during the period of the landlord's noncompliance and deduct the actual cost from rent — a targeted self-help remedy, not a blanket rent withholding right.

question: Under §76-1427, when a landlord's failure to provide essential services is deliberate rather than merely negligent, what additional remedy is available to the tenant?
choice_a: Punitive damages capped at $1,000
choice_b: Automatic termination of the lease with no notice required
choice_c: Recovery of substitute housing costs up to an amount equal to the periodic rent, plus reasonable attorney's fees
choice_d: A statutory doubling of the security deposit
explanation: Section 76-1427 provides that where the landlord's failure to supply essential services is deliberate, the tenant may recover the cost of reasonable substitute housing up to an amount equal to the periodic rent, in addition to diminution-of-value damages and reasonable attorney's fees.

question: Under §76-1423, how much notice must a Nebraska landlord generally give a tenant before entering the dwelling unit?
choice_a: No notice is required if the landlord owns the unit
choice_b: At least 7 days' notice
choice_c: At least 48 hours' notice, which may be given orally
choice_d: At least 24 hours' written notice of intent to enter, and entry only at reasonable times
explanation: Section 76-1423 requires the landlord to give the tenant at least 24 hours' written notice of intent to enter and to enter only at reasonable times, except where the tenant consents to shorter notice or in an emergency.

question: Under §76-1423, in which circumstance may a Nebraska landlord enter a dwelling unit without the tenant's consent or advance notice?
choice_a: In an emergency, or where the tenant has abandoned or surrendered the premises
choice_b: Whenever the landlord wants to show the unit to a potential buyer
choice_c: Anytime rent is more than 5 days late
choice_d: Only with prior written approval from the county sheriff
explanation: Section 76-1423 permits entry without consent only in an emergency or where the tenant has abandoned or surrendered the premises. Showing the unit to prospective buyers or tenants still requires the standard notice and reasonable-time requirements.

question: Under §76-1439, a Nebraska landlord is prohibited from retaliating against a tenant (for example, by raising rent or filing for possession) after the tenant does which of the following?
choice_a: Pays rent late once during the tenancy
choice_b: Complains in good faith to a government agency about a code violation, or joins or organizes a tenants' union
choice_c: Sublets the unit without permission
choice_d: Requests a copy of the signed lease
explanation: Section 76-1439 protects a tenant from retaliatory rent increases, service reductions, or eviction actions taken because the tenant complained in good faith to a code enforcement agency or organized/joined a tenants' union, subject to exceptions such as tenant-caused violations or rent default.

question: Nebraska's seller property condition disclosure statute, §76-2,120, requires the written disclosure statement to address which of the following, among others?
choice_a: Only the age of the roof
choice_b: Only whether the property has ever flooded
choice_c: The condition of electrical, heating, cooling, water, and sewer systems, known hazardous materials, title conditions such as easements or encroachments, and compliance with carbon monoxide alarm requirements
choice_d: Only the square footage and lot dimensions
explanation: Section 76-2,120 requires a written disclosure covering appliance functionality, electrical/heating/cooling/water/sewer systems, known material defects, hazardous substances, title conditions (easements, encroachments, zoning), utility connections, private transfer fee obligations, and carbon monoxide alarm compliance.

question: Under §76-2,120, by when must a Nebraska seller (or the seller's agent) deliver the property condition disclosure statement to the purchaser?
choice_a: At closing, along with the deed
choice_b: Within 10 days after the purchase agreement is signed
choice_c: Anytime before the purchaser takes possession
choice_d: On or before the effective date of any contract binding the purchaser to purchase the real property
explanation: Section 76-2,120 requires the disclosure statement, and any update, to be delivered to the purchaser or the purchaser's agent on or before the effective date of any contract that binds the purchaser to purchase the property — not merely by closing.

question: Which of the following transfers is specifically exempt from Nebraska's seller disclosure requirement under §76-2,120?
choice_a: Newly constructed residential real property that has never been occupied
choice_b: A sale of a 20-year-old single-family home
choice_c: A sale between unrelated first-time buyers and sellers
choice_d: A sale financed with a conventional mortgage
explanation: Section 76-2,120 exempts newly constructed residential real property that has never been occupied, along with other categories such as foreclosure/court-ordered sales and certain family or co-owner transfers. An ordinary resale between unrelated buyers, regardless of financing, is not exempt.

question: Section 76-2,120 exempts several categories of transfer from the disclosure requirement. Which pair below is correctly exempt?
choice_a: Sales by licensed real estate brokers and short sales
choice_b: Foreclosure or court-ordered sales, and transfers between certain family members or co-owners
choice_c: Cash sales and sales involving a home warranty
choice_d: Sales of condominiums and sales of manufactured homes
explanation: Among the exemptions listed in §76-2,120 are foreclosure and court-ordered transfers, transfers between co-owners, transfers between spouses or close family members, and transfers to government entities. Financing method, licensee involvement, and property type (condo/manufactured home) do not by themselves create an exemption.

question: If a Nebraska seller fails to comply with the §76-2,120 disclosure requirement, what recourse does the purchaser have, and within what time limit?
choice_a: The purchaser may rescind the sale at any time within 5 years
choice_b: The purchaser may only report the seller to the State Real Estate Commission for licensee discipline
choice_c: The purchaser may recover actual damages, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees, but must bring the action within one year after taking possession
choice_d: The conveyance is automatically void
explanation: Section 76-2,120 gives the purchaser a cause of action for actual damages, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees for noncompliance, but the action must be commenced within one year after the purchaser takes possession. The statute expressly states a transfer is not invalidated solely for noncompliance.

question: Nebraska's documentary stamp tax on real estate transfers, imposed under §76-901, is a tax on whom, and how is it evidenced?
choice_a: The tax is imposed on the grantee and evidenced by a recorded affidavit
choice_b: The tax is imposed equally on both parties and paid via a county invoice
choice_c: The tax is imposed on the real estate licensee facilitating the transaction
choice_d: The tax is imposed on the grantor executing the deed and evidenced by stamps affixed to the deed
explanation: Section 76-901 imposes the documentary stamp tax on the grantor executing the deed conveying the real estate, and the tax is evidenced by stamps attached to the deed at the register of deeds' office. All deeds are presumed taxable unless a statutory exemption under §76-902 applies.

question: Under §76-902, which of the following deeds is exempt from Nebraska's documentary stamp tax?
choice_a: A deed between spouses, or between a parent and child, made without consideration
choice_b: A deed transferring commercial property between unrelated LLCs for full consideration
choice_c: A deed conveying a newly platted subdivision lot to its first buyer
choice_d: A deed conveying property purchased at a private auction
explanation: Section 76-902 lists roughly two dozen exemption categories, including deeds between spouses, ex-spouses, and parent-child transfers made without consideration. Ordinary arm's-length sales for full consideration, including between LLCs or at auction, remain taxable.

question: Under §76-902, a deed that merely secures or releases a debt or other obligation (such as a mortgage or deed of trust) is treated how for documentary stamp tax purposes?
choice_a: Taxed at half the normal rate
choice_b: Exempt from the documentary stamp tax
choice_c: Taxed only if the underlying debt exceeds $50,000
choice_d: Subject to a flat $10 fee regardless of value
explanation: Section 76-902 exempts deeds which secure or release a debt or other obligation — meaning instruments like mortgages and deeds of trust that merely secure financing, rather than conveying beneficial ownership for consideration, do not trigger the documentary stamp tax.

question: Under the Nebraska Trust Deeds Act (§§76-1001 et seq.), how may a lender enforce a deed of trust upon a borrower's default, without a judicial foreclosure lawsuit?
choice_a: Nebraska does not permit any non-judicial foreclosure process
choice_b: Only by obtaining a confession of judgment signed at closing
choice_c: Through the trustee's power of sale, following statutory notice-of-default recording and waiting-period requirements
choice_d: By automatically transferring title to the lender 10 days after mailing a demand letter
explanation: The Nebraska Trust Deeds Act authorizes a trustee to exercise a power of sale conferred in the deed of trust, but only after recording a notice of default and observing the statutory waiting periods and notice-of-sale requirements — a non-judicial alternative to a mortgage foreclosure lawsuit.

question: Under §76-1006 of the Nebraska Trust Deeds Act, after a trustee records a notice of default, how long must the trustee generally wait before exercising the power of sale, and how does farm property change that period?
choice_a: At least 10 days generally, with no distinction for farm property
choice_b: At least six months in all cases
choice_c: There is no minimum waiting period once the notice of default is recorded
choice_d: At least one month generally, extended to at least two months if the property is subject to farming operations
explanation: Section 76-1006 requires the trustee to wait not less than one month after recording the notice of default before proceeding, extended to not less than two months where the notice of default involves property subject to farming operations, and farm debtors have additional cure rights under §76-1012.

question: Under §76-2,122, a real estate closing agent must deposit funds received on behalf of another party into a trust account at a federally insured institution, except for amounts up to what threshold that may be handled outside the trust account?
explanation: Section 76-2,122(2) requires a real estate closing agent to deposit funds received on behalf of another person into a trust account at a federally insured institution and to disburse closing funds only from that trust account, except that up to $1,500 may be handled or paid directly between parties without first passing through the trust account.

question: Under §76-2,122, what is the penalty for acting as a real estate closing agent in violation of the good-funds/trust-account requirements, and which transactions are exempt from the section?
choice_a: It is a Class IV felony; only all-cash transactions are exempt
choice_b: It is a Class V misdemeanor; condemnation/eminent domain transactions and lease or rental transactions are exempt
choice_c: It is a civil infraction only, with a fine but no criminal exposure; all residential transactions are exempt
choice_d: There is no penalty specified in the statute; commercial transactions are exempt
explanation: Section 76-2,122(5) makes a violation a Class V misdemeanor, and subsection (3) exempts transactions involving a political subdivision's exercise of condemnation or eminent domain, lease or rental transactions, and certain same-day back-to-back closings sharing a common principal and trust-account funds.
